Definition: compassion (in the plural); by extension, the womb (as cherishing the fetus); by implication, a maiden
BiblicalUsage: Racham is compassion — in the plural, compassions; and by extension, the womb, the place that cherishes what it carries. The true mother's bowels yearned upon her son before Solomon; Daniel confesses, 'To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses, though we have rebelled against him'; and Jeremiah says it is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe compassion is God's mother-heart toward us: He does not only forgive from a distance, He yearns over His people the way a mother yearns over the child she carried. That is why His mercies are new every morning — they are not a store He runs out of, but a womb that keeps bringing forth.
